description: Edit a document's Markdown. action: write | str_replace | cited_edits. write replaces the WHOLE document with `text`; str_replace swaps `find`→`replace` (set replace_all to change every occurrence) — prefer a small str_replace over a whole rewrite (`old_string`/`new_string` are the same as `find`/`replace`); cited_edits proposes several surgical edits at once (`edits`: [{old_string, new_string}], each old_string matching exactly once) with optional `citations` ([{n, doc_id, title, heading_path?, content?, table_id?, row_id?}]) that become footnotes when the edits land — the shape for grounded edits drawn from `retrieve`; a row is cited by its database's `doc_id` with its `table_id` and `row_id`; a citation's `doc_id` must be a document of this workspace you can read, else the whole edit is refused with `citation_not_found`. Changes are PROPOSED, never applied blindly: by default the tool returns `Proposed` and your change waits for the user to accept it — that is SUCCESS, never retry it. They are notified. The owner may instead have set the item to let AI edits apply directly, and then the result says `Applied`; or to be reviewed by a colleague, so someone other than the user accepts it. Never rewrite the document because your change looks missing: your reads include it, and `markdown` action:status reports what the user decided. Edits 3-way merge with concurrent human edits. `revises`: the ids of the CHANGES REQUESTED this proposal answers (from the block your reads open with); until a proposal names them, they keep leading your reads. ONE piece of work is ONE change, reviewed on one card: an ingest of a meeting or an email, or one Save to Stuga of several points. Give `change_title` (a few words naming its source, never a page's title) to your FIRST write for it, and pass the `change_id` the answer returns to EVERY later write for it, on every page and database; `change_summary` says what it does. A new page made inside a change, where AI edits wait for a colleague, stays visible only to the user and those who may approve it until it is approved. When your earlier change to a page is still undecided, a write there for another change waits behind it in a queue (`queued_behind`): that is SUCCESS, never retry it. Images written as ![alt](https://…) or as a data: URI are downloaded and stored with the document, so it never hotlinks; the Markdown title slot is the image's visible caption.

change_id.description: The `change_id` your first write for this piece of work returned: pass it to every later write for it.

change_summary.description: What the change does, in a sentence or two, for whoever approves it; a later write may replace it.

change_title.description: Opens a change for this piece of work and returns its `change_id`: a few words naming its source, as "Customer sync, 2026-10-21".

row_id.description: Citing a row of a database: the row's id, as `retrieve` or `query` gave it.

table_id.description: Citing a row of a database (`doc_id`): its table's id.

workspace_id.description: The workspace to act in: a `workspace_id` from `workspaces` action:list, which also says which node it is on.

name: markdown_edit
title: Edit a document
